migration_steps.activity: Establish PQC migration programme governance, inventory cryptographic assets (RSA-2048 at rest, ECDSA TLS 1.3 in transit, Java/Bouncy Castle usage), and define customer-facing compliance milestones for the 9-month deadline.
prerequisites: Access to AWS account, microservice inventory, and customer contract terms

migration_steps.activity: Engage the demanding customer (30% revenue) to agree a scoped PQC compliance definition: hybrid ML-KEM in TLS for their tenant, ML-DSA where signatures are under provider control, and a documented roadmap for KMS-dependent at-rest encryption pending AWS 2027 support.

Validate Bouncy Castle PQC provider versions in a Java Spring Boot staging environment: ML-KEM key establishment and ML-DSA signatures, including TLS hybrid integration via JSSE/provider configuration.
prerequisites: Bouncy Castle PQC-capable release identified and licensed

migration_steps.activity: Implement hybrid ML-KEM key establishment for TLS 1.3 on customer-facing ingress and service-to-service channels using Bouncy Castle, with classical fallback, in staging only.
prerequisites: Load balancer and service mesh TLS configuration change plan approved
Interoperability test matrix with customer clients defined

migration_steps.activity: Implement ML-DSA for provider-controlled digital signatures (e.g., internal service authentication tokens, audit log signing) in staging, keeping ML-KEM strictly for key establishment.
prerequisites: Key management design for ML-DSA keys outside AWS KMS documented

migration_steps.activity: Conduct security review, performance benchmarking, and interoperability testing of hybrid ML-KEM TLS and ML-DSA signatures in staging; produce evidence pack for customer.
Produce customer-facing PQC compliance report covering in-transit hybrid ML-KEM, ML-DSA signatures, and a dated roadmap for at-rest ML-KEM encryption contingent on AWS KMS 2027 support.
Deploy hybrid ML-KEM TLS and ML-DSA signature changes to production in a controlled rollout with classical fallback, respecting change freezes and zero-downtime constraints.
prerequisites: Step 7 customer acceptance of scoped compliance

migration_steps.activity: Design at-rest PQC encryption architecture using ML-KEM via AWS KMS, including envelope encryption and key hierarchy, as a design-only deliverable pending AWS KMS availability.
prerequisites: AWS KMS ML-KEM roadmap documentation obtained
Step 1 inventory of RSA-2048 at-rest usage

migration_steps.activity: Plan and schedule at-rest ML-KEM migration execution for after AWS KMS ML-KEM support is confirmed available and validated (earliest 2027), including re-encryption and key rotation.
prerequisites: AWS KMS ML-KEM support generally available and validated

blockers.blocker: AWS KMS does not currently support ML-KEM; announced support starts 2027.
blockers.reason: RSA-2048 encryption at rest is managed by AWS KMS, so post-quantum at-rest encryption cannot be implemented until KMS provides ML-KEM key wrapping.
blockers.resolution_required: Obtain written AWS roadmap confirmation, then validate ML-KEM KMS capability in staging once available; do not claim at-rest PQC compliance before validation.

blockers.blocker: Customer demands full PQC compliance within 9 months, but at-rest PQC depends on AWS KMS 2027.
blockers.reason: Full compliance including at-rest encryption is technically impossible within 9 months given the vendor timeline.
blockers.resolution_required: Negotiate a scoped compliance definition covering in-transit hybrid ML-KEM and ML-DSA signatures now, with a contractual roadmap for at-rest PQC.

blockers.blocker: Bouncy Castle PQC support must be validated for the specific Java Spring Boot runtime and TLS stack.
blockers.reason: Library capability does not guarantee production-grade interoperability, performance, or FIPS alignment.
blockers.resolution_required: Complete staging proof of concept and performance benchmarking; obtain Bouncy Castle release notes and support statements.

blockers.blocker: Production rollout must respect change freezes and zero-downtime constraints.
blockers.reason: TLS and signature changes affect all 5,000 customers and cannot cause outages.
blockers.resolution_required: Change advisory board approval, canary rollout plan, and tested rollback with classical fallback.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Announced ML-KEM support starting 2027; not currently available or validated.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Written AWS roadmap confirmation and, when available, KMS ML-KEM API documentation and staging validation results.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: PQC-capable Java library with ML-KEM and ML-DSA support claimed; specific version compatibility with the provider's Java Spring Boot stack unconfirmed.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Release notes, supported algorithm list, and successful staging interoperability and performance test results.

vendor_dependencies.pqc_support_status: Hybrid ML-KEM TLS integration depends on runtime and provider configuration; not confirmed for the provider's exact version.
vendor_dependencies.evidence_required: Vendor documentation and staging TLS handshake test evidence.

algorithm_roles.ML-KEM: Post-quantum key establishment for TLS 1.3 in-transit encryption (hybrid with classical) and, once AWS KMS supports it, for encryption-at-rest key wrapping.
algorithm_roles.ML-DSA: Post-quantum digital signatures for provider-controlled authentication tokens, audit log signing, and other signature use cases; not used for key establishment.

raw_response.confidence: Medium: in-transit hybrid ML-KEM and ML-DSA signatures can likely be delivered within 9 months using Bouncy Castle, subject to staging validation; at-rest PQC is blocked on AWS KMS 2027 support and cannot be completed within the customer deadline.
